Forecast with the forecast package's forecast() generic

Source: R/forecast_pkg.R
forecast.timestral_model.Rd

Registered as an S3 method for forecast::forecast() when the forecast package is loaded, so forecast::forecast(m, AirPassengers, h = 24) forecasts a ts with a Timestral model and returns a "forecast" object. It calls timestral_forecast() and then timestral_as_forecast(); see that page for the interval levels.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'timestral_model'
forecast(object, y, h, level = c(80, 98), variate = 1L, ...)

Arguments

object

a timestral_model from timestral_load()

y

the series to forecast, a ts (a univariate ts, or an mts whose columns are forecast jointly; pick the column with variate)

h

horizon in steps (required)

level

interval levels in percent, each pairing two quantile knots

variate

which variate of a multivariate y to return

...

further arguments to timestral_forecast(), such as covariates or symmetric; other forecast-generic arguments (fan, lambda, biasadj, ...) are rejected

Value

An object of class "forecast".

Examples

m <- timestral_load(system.file("extdata", "tiny", package = "timestralR"))
if (requireNamespace("forecast", quietly = TRUE))
  forecast::forecast(m, AirPassengers, h = 12)
